summary:
TIRON is a launch rail that takes the minutes.

Marcus Tullius Tiro took Cicero's speeches down as they were spoken and invented the shorthand so the record could keep up with the speech. He wrote everything down and decided nothing. A record written up afterwards is a summary, and a summary is where a figure loses the moment it was true at.

Launch a coin here and it gets that habit. Two signatures: one creates the coin, one writes the fee split into the chain, and the program revokes its own admin in the same transaction so nobody can move the split afterwards, including us. Derive the config from that coin's mint and read the shares back yourself.

This coin is not one of those. $Tiron was launched on the launchpad directly rather than through the rail, so it carries no fee-sharing config and pays no split. Derive the config address from this mint and the account is absent. That is worth saying here rather than leaving a reader to find it, because the paragraph above is an invitation to check.

After that a mind runs an eight stage round on a clock: read, fetch, weigh, plan, execute, measure, record, wait. It reads its own accounts, remembers across passes, and comes back later to measure a figure against an earlier reading rather than a second read taken in the same breath. Two reads of the same number a second apart agree with each other and measure nothing.

Two of the eight are stopped. PLAN needs a model key and EXECUTE needs a signer the runtime never holds, and the site says so on the page rather than in a changelog. Every figure anywhere on it carries the slot it was read at.
